statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 68 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 33 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour twenty-one: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, an unresolved hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2-year at 4.35% and September hike odds near a coin flip
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about six hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to roughly 4.350 percent, its highest in a month, against the Federal Reserve H.15 reading of 4.20 percent for 27 August, while the 10-year moved to about 4.72 percent from 4.67 percent, and September rate-hike odds were repriced to roughly 57 to 61 percent from about 34 percent, leaving the meeting described in current reporting as close to a coin flip. The decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor industry fell 2.91 percent and semiconductor equipment 3.96 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Sector context was split, with Technology about 1.4 percent lower against Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical each about 1.4 percent higher. The same repricing was expressed in a dollar index gain of roughly 0.6 percent to near 99.66 and a gold decline of more than 2.5 percent from a 4,629 dollar high, while crude softened with WTI settling at 83.40 dollars, down 0.16 percent in an 82.25 to 83.78 dollar range, with no verified new Middle East supply discontinuity. The shared cross-asset context file read this run was collected at 14:42 UTC, beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and the assessment rests on independent primary-source verification; its delayed readings of Treasury futures lower across the curve and a higher volatility future were directionally consistent but are explicitly not usable as live price-path evidence. Weekend headline flow through the assessment cutoff has been thematic rather than index-moving, with no verified geopolitical or policy discontinuity. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path and no venue is open to produce one, Tail is 5 in every hour of this window and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window; Stress runs 25 to 33 in the moderate band purely as a measure of information waiting to be priced at the reopen and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence steps down from 68 to 62 as a function of tape age rather than conflicting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final three hours of Friday's cash session and the first twenty-one hours of the weekend halt. The mode was event/whipsaw as the Jackson Hole keynote was digested, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 17:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. Every hour of this window has a published assessment. The twenty-one halt hours sit at a flat Tail of 5 to 8 with Stress in the low to mid twenties, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 69 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 33 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year near 4.35 percent and September hike odds around 57 to 61 percent, Friday's narrow semiconductor-led decline with the semiconductor industry down 2.91 percent against five of eight megacaps higher, the dollar and gold moves that expressed the same repricing, the softer crude path near 83 dollars WTI, Broadcom's fiscal Q3 report scheduled after the close on 2 September, and the 1 to 4 September data stack running from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS through ADP and ISM Services to Nonfarm Payrolls. Confidence eases from 68 to 62 as the reference tape ages. The first genuine price-path evidence arrives at the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, roughly six hours after the final slot of this window.
